title: Find the MUX by its name, every time

blocks.text: `PaymentService` sends purchases through whatever Q2 has deployed under a name it is given, such as `acquirer-mux`. It is created when the application starts and then runs for weeks. In that time the operations team edits the descriptors: they change a timeout and Q2 redeploys the file, or they add a second link and give the old name to a pool. They expect the service to keep working through all of it without a restart.
Write `mux()` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PaymentService.java`. `pay(...)` already handles a `null` from it as "unavailable". About five lines.
The tests do what Q2 does with a descriptor, without a Q2: they create the component, register it under its name, start it, and stop and destroy it on a redeploy.

cases.says: with a QMUX deployed under the name, a purchase goes through it and is approved
a service created before the MUX is deployed finds it once it is, because the name is looked up when it is used
after a redeploy the name refers to a new QMUX, and a reference kept from before is a stopped one
the code depends on the MUX interface only, so a MUXPool can take the name's place

origin.section: 4.7 Code Names a MUX and Never Keeps One

concepts: Code looks a MUX up by name when it uses it and depends only on the MUX interface, so it survives late deployment and redeploys, and a pool can take the name.
